problem: The second sentence is self-contradictory and will confuse a student. The cabin gauge reading IS the differential pressure, so "the differential is much larger than the cabin gauge reading alone" cannot be true. The point being made is that the differential is much larger than it would be at sea level, or much larger than the outside ambient pressure.
fix: Using absolute cabin pressure instead of differential pressure. At 11 km altitude the outside pressure is only about 23 kPa, so a cabin held near 75 kPa absolute gives a differential of about 50–55 kPa — close to the full cabin pressure. At sea level the same cabin would give almost no differential at all.

problem: The symbol r is used for two different things: the mean skin radius in p r / t and I ≈ π r³ t, and the distance from the neutral axis in σ_b = M r / I. In the worked example the same number 1.2 m is used for both, which only works because the outer fibre is taken at the mean radius.
fix: Use y for the distance from the neutral axis: σ_b = M y / I, with y in m. State that for the thin skin y is taken as the mean radius r, so the numbers in the example are unchanged.

problem: The applied moment is called "ultimate" but the stress is compared with yield (345 MPa). Standard practice compares limit-load stress with yield and ultimate-load stress with ultimate strength (about 1.5 times yield for 2024 aluminium).
fix: Say either "the ultimate-load stress of 45.2 MPa is well below the ultimate strength of about 470 MPa, and the limit-load stress would be about two-thirds of this, well below the 345 MPa yield", or drop the word "ultimate" from the bending moment.

problem: Routing the tailplane load through the fin root is only correct when the tailplane is mounted on the fin (T-tail). On a conventional tail the tailplane attaches directly to the rear fuselage frames.
fix: Label the middle node "Tailplane root / fin root attachment" and note in the caption that on a T-tail the load passes through the fin, while on a conventional tail it goes straight into rear fuselage frames.

problem: The divisor 8.686 × 10⁻³ is written without brackets, so read left to right the line looks like 200 000 × 1.2 / 8.686 × 10⁻³, which is ambiguous.
Cross-references to Chapter 1.1 and Chapter 1.9 are plain text, not links, so a student reading on a phone cannot jump to them.
fix: Write them as Chapter 1.1 and Chapter 1.9.
